caption: Newanforbi v. AT&T, et al.
court: San Joaquin Sup. Ct. (potential; venue and employer entity unconfirmed)
claims: Rescinded Employment Offer — Promissory Estoppel / Breach (investigation); FEHA National-Origin / Language Discrimination (administrative-exhaustion review); FCRA / ICRAA and Fair Chance Act (contingent on proof of background-information use)
status: PRE-FILING EVIDENCE REVIEW — AT&T issued a written offer for requisition R-106742 on May 28, 2026, initiated Workday onboarding and a First Advantage screening, then recruiter Richard Patterson texted approximately two hours later that the manager would not proceed because the role needed a Spanish speaker and Plaintiff did not pass the Spanish assessment. No complaint or administrative charge has been drafted or filed. The current record does not establish acceptance, detrimental reliance, a completed consumer report, use of criminal/registry information, or discriminatory motive.
note: Do not draft from the present record. First obtain the formal offer, Spanish score/rating, candidate-history audit, application statuses, screening file, and employing-entity identity.
defendants: Potential employer defendant presently identified only by the record as “AT&T” / “AT&T Non Management” (precise employing entity and owner/operator of the Lodi store must be confirmed; do not assume parent AT&T Inc. employed Plaintiff); Richard Patterson (AT&T recruiter and percipient witness, not presently identified as a proposed defendant); First Advantage (screening vendor, factual participant only unless its file shows actionable reporting conduct); DOES 1–20
causes: [INVESTIGATE] Promissory Estoppel — written May 28 offer and immediate onboarding prompts; requires proof of a clear promise, reasonable detrimental reliance, and resulting loss
[INVESTIGATE] Breach of Written or Implied Contract / Implied Covenant — contingent on obtaining the formal offer, proving acceptance, and identifying any conditions or at-will language

[WEAK ON PRESENT RECORD] FEHA National-Origin / Ancestry Discrimination (Gov. Code § 12940) — language can operate as a national-origin proxy, but Spanish fluency appears facially job-related for the expressly bilingual role and the recruiter identified a failed proficiency assessment as the reason

[CONTINGENT] California Fair Chance Act (Gov. Code § 12952) — only if AT&T considered conviction history before a conditional offer or rescinded because of it without the required assessment/notices; no present exhibit shows such use

[CONTINGENT] FCRA (15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)) and ICRAA (Civ. Code § 1786 et seq.) — First Advantage invited screening after the offer, but no report, disclosure/authorization, pre-adverse notice, or screening-based decision is presently in the record

[CONTINGENT / NO PRESENT FACTUAL BASIS] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E) and related UCL theory — preserve only if the screening file proves employment use of Megan’s Law registry information; timing and the recruiter’s express Spanish-test explanation currently point elsewhere
key_facts: On May 16, 2026, Plaintiff submitted two AT&T applications: R-107776 Retail Sales Consultant at Stockton Pacific (5756 Pacific Ave. #94, Stockton) at 1:15 p.m., and R-106742 Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant at Lodi (2439 W. Kettleman Ln.) at 2:31 p.m. AT&T immediately advanced both applications. The Stockton track generated a Virtual Job Tryout and an interview invitation; the Lodi track generated an interview invitation. The original Stockton interview was set for May 19 at 4:45 p.m. but was canceled at 3:46 p.m. that day and rescheduled for May 22 at 10:30 a.m. The original Lodi interview was set for May 20 at 2:00 p.m. but was canceled at 1:51 p.m. and rescheduled for May 21 at 2:00 p.m. Reminder emails document the rescheduled appointments, but the exhibits do not independently prove attendance or what was said in either interview. On May 22 at 11:11 a.m., AT&T’s language-testing provider directed Plaintiff to complete a pre-employment assessment within five days for Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant position 16000025. At 11:37 a.m., Language Testing International provided access code 82594911 for an ACTFL Telephone OPIc Spanish speaking test expiring May 25 at midnight and stated that the rating would be provided to AT&T Taleo. The file does not include the test recording, score, proficiency threshold, score report, retest policy as applied, or evidence of who reviewed the result. On May 28 at 10:13 a.m., AT&T Workday sent “Welcome to the team,” stating it was “excited to officially offer” Plaintiff R-106742 and directing him to review and accept the formal offer in Candidate Home. Workday then sent offer-process tasks at 10:15, 10:16, and 10:17 a.m. to review documents, change government identifiers, and change personal information. At 10:19 a.m., First Advantage stated that “AT&T Non Management” had contracted for screening services and invited Plaintiff to provide information, review FCRA rights, and optionally complete ID.me identity verification. At 12:23 p.m., a text shown under recruiter Richard Patterson’s AT&T contact stated: “Unfortunately, the manager advised me that he no longer wants to move forward with your offer. He stated that he need a Spanish speaker and you did not pass the Spanish assessment. Sorry for the inconvenience.” Plaintiff replied: “No worries sir, thank you for the opportunity.” The sequence proves an offer followed by an almost immediate rescission and an express stated reason. It does not prove that Plaintiff opened or accepted the formal offer, completed onboarding or screening, incurred reliance expenses, left other work, lost alternative employment, or received any First Advantage report or adverse-action notice.
procedural_status: Intake / evidence-preservation stage only. No pleading, demand, CRD charge, or court filing exists. Before choosing a forum or defendant, obtain: (1) the complete Workday offer and all attachments/conditions; (2) acceptance and task audit logs; (3) the R-106742 and R-107776 candidate-history/status logs; (4) the job postings and minimum Spanish standard; (5) the ACTFL OPIc recording, rating, rubric, transmission date, and AT&T decision notes; (6) Patterson’s full SMS thread and communications with the hiring manager; (7) interview attendance notes and scorecards; (8) the complete First Advantage/ID.me file, including disclosure, authorization, report, status, and cancellation reason; (9) identity of the legal employer and Lodi store operator; and (10) documents showing any reliance or wage loss. If a FEHA theory remains supportable after that review, calendar the CRD exhaustion period independently; use May 28, 2026 as the conservative accrual date and do not rely on the portfolio entry as a deadline calculation.
damages: Unvalued. The exhibits establish no wage rate, scheduled start date, accepted offer, work schedule, reliance expenditure, foregone job, or duration of expected employment. At-will employment and mitigation would substantially limit expectancy damages. Emotional distress is not documented. Reserve damages at $0 in portfolio analytics until the formal offer and actual reliance/loss proof are obtained; do not import statutory values from the separate registry-background-check matters without evidence that AT&T or First Advantage used registry information here.
risk: High-risk / not complaint-ready. The strongest evidence is the tight May 28 sequence and the recruiter’s contemporaneous statement identifying the decisionmaker’s reason. That same statement is also the principal defense evidence: Spanish speaking ability is facially central to a position expressly titled “Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant,” and a validated proficiency screen can be a legitimate, nondiscriminatory hiring criterion. The strongest non-discrimination theory is process-based promissory estoppel, but it fails without acceptance/reliance and measurable detriment; a written offer may also contain express contingencies and at-will language. Contract liability is similarly contingent on the missing offer terms. FCRA/ICRAA, Fair Chance Act, and Penal Code § 290.46 theories are presently speculative: the invitation to begin a First Advantage task does not show that a report was completed or used, and AT&T’s express reason points to the Spanish test. The timing nevertheless warrants preservation because screening was initiated minutes after the offer and before rescission. Do not plead the parent corporation, recruiter, testing vendor, or screening vendor without evidence tying each entity to a legal duty and the decision.
